claims: Old cached snapshots turn into "unavailable" instead of being refreshed. `ui-dashboard/src/app/cdps/[symbol]/troves/[troveId]/_lib/trove-og-data.ts:273-274` — once cache entry is more than 5 minutes old, `unstable_cache` hands back the old entry; line 274 fails the age check and returns `null` without waiting for that refresh

Why it's half done: commit 71816493 added the per-key in-flight map (`inFlightFetches`, lines 237-252) ... The refresh itself was never added, so today the map only merges concurrent first-time fetches.

Why tests didn't catch it: the `unstable_cache` mock in `_lib/__tests__/trove-og-data.test.ts:12-25` just calls the function, so no old entry is ever served; the test at lines 227-239 only checks the `troveOgDataIsFresh` helper on its own

Any text in the URL's symbol ends up on the branded image. `opengraph-image.tsx:29-37` → `_og/trove-og-card.tsx:172-178`, and the alt text at `opengraph-image.tsx:44-45` — card shows `decodeParam(params.symbol).toUpperCase()` with no check and no length limit
A long string also overflows the 360px left column.
"Not found" is cached. `trove-og-data.ts:203, 212-214` — a trove shared right after it opens, before it's indexed, gets `null` cached for 60s
That `null` has no timestamp, so the fix for finding 1 can't age it out. The next request after a quiet period gets the cached `null` again.
`trove-og-data.ts:184` has an "Exported for focused data-contract tests" comment on a function that isn't exported.

judge_reasoning.3882085361: The review discusses resolveMetadataBase trusting x-forwarded-host but calls it fine and not an issue. It does not flag the missing allowlist as a defect.
judge_reasoning.3882086206: The review says icrTone matches icrTextClass, and does so under 'Checked and fine'. It never flags the duplication.
judge_reasoning.3882090788: The review never mentions IPv6 loopback or [::1] handling.
judge_reasoning.3882119274: The review never raises the concern that event-time ICR is shown as a fresh health signal.
judge_reasoning.3882119284: The review's finding 1 is about stale entries returning null or unavailable. It does not cover the combined data age plus image cache age (about 11 minutes of staleness); it even calls the revalidate/SWR config fine.

1.why: trove-og-data.ts:254-274: unstable_cache uses revalidate 60s and serves the old entry while it refreshes in the background, so once fetchedAtMs is over 5 min old (line 23), line 274 returns null and the card shows 'unavailable'.

2.why: The history is accurate: inFlightFetches (lines 237-252) was added in 71816493 and only merges concurrent calls. But this is background for claim 1, not a separate defect.

3.why: The test file's mock at lines 12-25 returns fn unchanged, so no old entry is ever served, and the freshness test at ~227-239 only calls troveOgDataIsFresh directly. That is a verified test gap for defect 1.

4.why: routeIdentity (opengraph-image.tsx:29-37) decodes the symbol without checking it. When data is null the card uses identity (card:434,480), and IdentityPill shows symbol.toUpperCase() at card:173. The alt text at :44-45 does the same, with no length limit.

5.why: IdentityPill sits in the 360px-wide left column (card:457,480). IDENTITY_PILL_STYLE (card:28-39) has no maxWidth, overflow or ellipsis, so a long symbol overflows.

6.why: fetchTroveOgData returns null inside the cached function when no collateral or trove is found (lines 203, 212-214), so unstable_cache stores 'not found' for 60s.

7.why: The null result has no fetchedAtMs, and line 274 only checks the age of non-null data. After a quiet period the old cached null is served again while the refresh runs in the background.

8.why: trove-og-data.ts:184 says '@internal Exported for focused data-contract tests' above `async function fetchTroveOgData`, which is not exported. The comment is misleading.

9.why: page.tsx:48-50 defines its own shortTroveId, identical to the exported one at trove-og-card.tsx:115-117, instead of importing it.
